body:
**Blocked by:** none
**Model tier:** low

## Context

Model tier rationale: This applies the same affected-row guard at two existing test-fixture UPDATE sites in one file.

- PR #1123, finding `ec01677db8`, `backend/packages/data/src/trash/__tests__/purgeExpiredTrashPerTenant.test.ts:39`: trash discards the backdate UPDATE result, so a wrong database/item pair silently skips fixture setup.
- PR #1123, finding `ee2bfc6bdd`, `backend/packages/data/src/trash/__tests__/purgeExpiredTrashPerTenant.test.ts:81`: makeFilesItem discards the file-property UPDATE result, so an absent item silently loses the blob association.
- PR #1123, finding `4e623975d4`, `backend/packages/data/src/trash/__tests__/purgeExpiredTrashPerTenant.test.ts:39`: This duplicates the unguarded trash backdate; unexpected tenant visibility can also turn it into a silent zero-row write.

## Task

Require exactly one affected row from each of the two targeted fixture UPDATEs: the backdate in `trash` and the blob-property assignment in `makeFilesItem`. Fail at the helper with a diagnostic naming the helper and item when the affected-row result is not one. Add focused zero-row-result checks for both helpers using narrowly scoped query-result doubles that intercept only the targeted fixture UPDATE, and restore the doubles even when assertions fail. Keep real choke-point creation/deletion and the existing real-database purge scenarios.

## Touches

- backend/packages/data/src/trash/__tests__/purgeExpiredTrashPerTenant.test.ts (trash/makeFilesItem UPDATE checks and focused fixture failure cases only)

## Scope

### In scope

One checked-write convention at the two reported fixture sites; the two trash findings share one fix.

### Out of scope

Production purge behavior, unrelated UPDATEs, transaction/scope policy changes and a shared fixture framework.

## Acceptance criteria

- For finding `ec01677db8`, a zero-row backdate rejects in trash with the affected item identified, before any purge assertion can run.
- For finding `ee2bfc6bdd`, a zero-row blob-property update rejects in makeFilesItem with the affected item identified instead of returning a successfully configured item.
- For finding `4e623975d4`, trash also refuses a zero-row result representing an invisible item; the existing tenant-scoped successful purge cases still pass with both guards enabled.
